summary: Researched AI coding agents w/ orchestration vs our task-graph daemon. KEY VERDICT: Heavy overlap with Claude Code's NATIVE Agent Teams (experimental, v2.1.32+): it already has a shared task list w/ pending/in-progress/completed states, typed task DEPENDENCIES that auto-unblock, file-locking task CLAIM, a mailbox, AND hook-based enforcement (TaskCreated/TaskCompleted/TeammateIdle, exit-2 gating) — these directly duplicate our claim-before-edit gate, dependency edges, and complete_task summaries. Our genuine differentiators vs native: (1) persistent CROSS-SESSION/CROSS-WORKSPACE task graph w/ ghost edges (native task list is per-team, ephemeral, no resumption, one-team-at-a-time, stored in ~/.claude/tasks/{team}); (2) typed CONTEXT edges + two-tier context handoff (native only has blocking deps); (3) live web DASHBOARD/DAG viz (native is terminal/tmux panes only); (4) PreToolUse prompt-classifying router + always-on gate (native gate exists but is team-scoped). Competitors: Devin 2.0 (parallel cloud VMs, Mission/Spaces planning UI, editable task plans, arch diagrams), Cursor 2.0 (≤8 parallel agents, cursor.com/agents dashboard, branch isolation), GitHub Copilot coding agent (cloud, git-worktree-isolated parallel, "Mission Control"/"My Work" unified dashboard), Factory.ai droids (thousands parallel, Mission Control view), OpenHands (AgentDelegateAction parallel sub-agents + sequential TaskToolSet, open SDK), Roo Code (Boomerang/Orchestrator mode — SEQUENTIAL only, parallel is open enhancement req), Cline (delegation), Aider (architect/editor 2-model, NO native parallel/tracking), Windsurf Cascade (planning mode, no task graph). NO competitor offers a persistent cross-workspace DAG w/ typed context edges + hook enforcement as a layer on top — that combo + cross-workspace ghost edges is our defensible niche, but single-workspace orchestration + dashboard is increasingly commoditized natively.
